quote: This identifies 11 proteins with causal evidence of involvement in human disease that have not previously been targeted, including EGF, IL-16, PAPPA, SPON1, F3, ADM, CASP-8, CHI3L1, CXCL16, GDF15 and MMP-12.
summary: Proteome-wide Mendelian randomization flags CHI3L1 among proteins with causal evidence in disease; no UC-specific result or direction.

quote: It plays a major role in tissue injury, inflammation, tissue repair, and remodeling responses.
summary: Review of CHI3L1 function, receptors and roles in inflammation and cancer, with no new data.

quote: The ability of interleukin13 to induce tissue inflammation and fibrosis was also markedly diminished in the absence of BRP-39.
summary: Mouse Chi3l1 (BRP-39) knockout reduces Th2 and IL-13-driven lung inflammation and fibrosis; not a colitis model.

quote: ELISA revealed significant elevation of CHI3L1 in the CSF of multiple sclerosis (MS) patients as well as mild elevation with aging.
summary: CHI3L1 is raised in CSF and astrocytes in neurological diseases; no gut data.
GP39 here is CD40 ligand (anti-gp39 antibody), not CHI3L1.

quote: In conclusion, CHI3L1 expressed in colon cancer cells promotes cancer cell proliferation, macrophage recruitment and angiogenesis.
summary: CHI3L1 overexpression or knockdown in colon cancer cells changes macrophage recruitment, chemokine secretion and tumor growth; colorectal cancer, not UC.

quote: CHI3L1 plays a pathogenic role in colitis, presumably by enhancing the adhesion and invasion of bacteria on/into CEC.
summary: CHI3L1 is induced in inflamed mucosa including UC, and anti-CHI3L1 antibody reduced bacterial invasion and DSS colitis.
Synovial histology paper; gp39 appears only as an MHC-peptide complex stain, with no CHI3L1 result.

quote: Genes involved in carbohydrate and lipid metabolism were up-regulated in helminth-colonized tissue, whereas tissues with active colitis showed up-regulation of proinflammatory genes such as IL-17, IL-13RA2, and CHI3L1.
summary: CHI3L1 is one of the proinflammatory genes up in active UC mucosa of a single helminth-treated patient.

quote: Increased serum CHI3L1 also correlates with disease severity in rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, liver fibrosis, inflammatory bowel disease, and bacterial septicemia.
summary: Review of CHI3L1 as a disease marker, noting higher serum levels with severity in several diseases including IBD.

quote: Using proteomic analysis of postmortem cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and brain tissue from the simian immunodeficiency virus primate model, we demonstrate here a specific increase in YKL-40 that was tightly associated with lentiviral encephalitis.
summary: YKL-40 rises in CSF in SIV encephalitis and may mark it; unrelated to UC.
gp39 appears only as an MHC-HC gp39 complex stain in synovium; no CHI3L1 result.
gp39 here means CD40 ligand, not CHI3L1.

quote: In this review, we describe the role of CHI3L1 in inducing pro-inflammatory/pro-tumorigenic and angiogenic factors that could promote tumor growth and metastasis.
summary: Short review on CHI3L1 driving pro-inflammatory and angiogenic factors in cancer.

quote: Here we demonstrate that CHI3L1 (aka Brp39) knockout (KO) mice treated with azoxymethane (AOM)/dextran sulphate sodium (DSS) developed severe colitis but lesser incidence of CAC as compared to that in wild-type (WT) mice.
summary: Chi3l1 knockout mice develop more severe colitis but less colitis-associated cancer, so it protects epithelium yet promotes tumor growth.

quote: YKL-40/chitinase-3-like-1 protein is often up-regulated in inflammation-associated diseases.
summary: Mini-review on YKL-40 enhancing inflammation and tumor progression.

quote: In mouse strains with genetic deletions of Chi3l1 or Sema7a, there was a significant reduction in pulmonary metastasis.
summary: Chi3l1 deletion or antiserum reduces melanoma lung metastasis in mice; cancer study, not colitis.

quote: In conclusion, CBM region of CHI3L1 is critical in activating Akt signaling in CECs, and the activation may be associated with the development of chronic colitis.
summary: Mutating the chitin-binding motif of CHI3L1 in colonic epithelial cells reduces Akt activation and IL-8 and TNF-alpha secretion.

quote: Inhibition of CHI3L1 by anti-CHI3L1 antibody or CHI3L1-specific short interfering RNA reduced the adhesion of CBP21-overexpressing E. coli to CECs.
summary: CHI3L1 enhances bacterial adhesion to colonic epithelial cells; blocking or silencing it reduces adhesion.

quote: Here, we demonstrated that circulating CHI3L1 levels are higher in HPS patients with pulmonary fibrosis compared with those who remain fibrosis free, and that these levels associate with disease severity.
summary: Circulating CHI3L1 tracks fibrosis severity in Hermansky-Pudlak lung disease; not a gut study.

quote: In summary, CHI3L1 may contribute to the proliferation, migration, and neoplastic progression of CECs under inflammatory conditions and could be a useful biomarker for neoplastic changes in patients with IBD.
summary: CHI3L1 expression is higher in colonic mucosa of IBD patients with dysplasia or cancer and is proposed as a neoplasia marker.

quote: CSF chitinase levels were significantly increased in patients with RRMS and NMO compared with HCs and patients with SPMS and OIND.
summary: CHI3L1 is one of three chitinases measured in MS and NMO CSF; no UC data.

quote: Animal studies using BRP-39 null mutant mice demonstrated that BRP-39 was required for optimal allergen sensitization and Th2 inflammation.
summary: Review of BRP-39/YKL-40 in asthma and allergy, including CHI3L1 polymorphisms and knockout mice.

quote: We demonstrate that CSF YKL-40 levels are elevated after acute TBI, and that YKL-40 levels are higher in patients who died following injury than in patients who survived.
summary: YKL-40 is elevated in CSF after traumatic brain injury and tracks outcome; no UC data.

quote: Anti-CHI3L1 antibodies or pan-chitinase inhibitors may have the potential to suppress CHI3L1-mediated chronic inflammation and the subsequent carcinogenic change in epithelial cells.
summary: Review of CHI3L1 in IBD-associated inflammation and epithelial carcinogenesis, suggesting it as a therapeutic target.
